title: Check yourself: The automation boundary, needed accuracy and the pilot

questions.stem: Scenario: Ridgeway Credit wants an autonomous agent that approves loan disbursements end to end, and the sponsor is eager to start. What should the architect establish first?

options.text: Which model tier will run the approval steps, so that the cost of the project can be estimated early in planning
options.says: Ruled out because the model comes after the boundary, and the page says to "Keep with a person" decisions that carry accountability.

options.text: How many tokens one disbursement review is expected to consume across all the steps
options.says: Ruled out because cost is downstream of the same question, and the page asks "who answers for it, and could a person have caught it?".

options.text: Whether the build can be completed inside the quarter that the sponsor has proposed
options.says: Ruled out because a schedule is not among the facts the page says to establish before promising anything: "the boundary, the number and the scale".

options.text: Which decisions carry accountability for the lender and so have to stay with a person
options.says: Where accountability sits fixes what may be automated at all, and everything else follows from that boundary.

origin.section: The automation boundary and who is accountable

questions.stem: Scenario: Alder Health's ten-user pilot of a note-summarising assistant went well, and the business now wants it for two thousand clinicians. What should the architect raise first?

options.text: The cost of the additional licences for the two thousand new users
options.says: Ruled out because licences are a consequence and not a risk, and a roll-out plan "that lists licence counts is not" a plan.

options.text: Which friendly conditions of the trial will not carry over to everyone
options.says: Scale changes the surroundings, so the first contribution is naming the assumptions that held only in friendly conditions.

options.text: Whether a larger and more capable model should replace the smaller one that was used in the pilot
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "None of the rows is about the model getting worse".

options.text: The training timetable for the clinicians who will start using it
options.says: Ruled out because training addresses a later step, while the page asks for the assumptions to be named "before the roll-out, not after the first incident".

origin.section: From a pilot to the full population
